title: Compute brief - 29 October 2026
description: Google Cloud revenue doubles to $30.7 billion with a $561 billion backlog, and Google is now renting third-party capacity to keep up. Microsoft's Azure grows 48% but capex lands at $45.2 billion, below its own $50 billion plan, because outside capacity arrived late. Samsung says its 2027 HBM is sold out. The UK sets a 6 GW by 2030 target with grid priority for data centres that sign its covenant. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The hyperscalers have more orders than buildings
lede: The constraint in last night's earnings was delivery, not demand. Alphabet said Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion with TPU system sales a meaningful contributor, and its backlog reached $561 billion, just over 55% of which it expects to book within 24 months. Because supply is tight, Google began using third-party compute at the end of the third quarter and will ramp it in the fourth, at a margin cost. Microsoft grew Azure 48% and commercial remaining performance obligation 73% to $677 billion, but spent $45.2 billion on capex and finance leases against a $50 billion plan because some third-party capacity deliveries slipped, and it said some GPU-as-a-service contracts moved to the second half. This morning Samsung said its 2027 HBM volume is sold out at target prices, a day after SK hynix said the same of more than half its 2027 and 2028 capacity. In London the Budget put a number on sovereign demand: 6 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2030, with grid capacity reserved for sites that meet the new covenant. On the public tape all 70 list prints confirmed; Lambda H100 holds at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69 per GPU-hour.
